COEUR D’ALENE, Idaho – Beginning in November 2026, and continuing through December 2026, the BLM in coordination with the US Wildland Fire Service will conduct a series of prescribed burns across northern Idaho on Bureau of Land Management lands. These prescribed burns aim to reduce hazardous fuel accumulations, enhance forest health and landscape resiliency, protect wildlife habitats, and improve firefighter and public safety by reducing wildfire risks. Burn activities, listed below, will proceed as weather, staffing, and on-ground conditions allow; acreages are approximate: Coeur d'Alene Field Office Blackwell Hand Piles (4 acres) – Coeur d’Alene, ID. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn BLM Fishing Derby brings Americans Outside for recreation and stewardship in Imperial Valley, California Oct 13, 2026 In a region best known for its off-highway vehicle adventures, the BLM California's El Centro Field Office hooked a different type of recreator for its second annual Fishing Derby Cast and Clean-up event. More than 100 members of the local community gathered for the event on Saturday, Sept. 26, bringing together recreation, community engagement, and public-land stewardship on BLM-managed public lands in Imperial County, California. The fishing derby took place at the Hot Springs Long-Term Visitor Area and on BLM-managed lands adjacent to the Highline and All-American canals. For many attendees, it was their first fishing opportunity, and several first-time anglers caught their first fish. Reducing vegetation along roads can create a break in fuels, giving firefighters another option if conditions change. It is the underlying technology for many cryptocurrency systems, but it can also be used in other types of applications. A blockchain is the ledger itself. It contains transactional records that are grouped into blocks. Each block is cryptographically linked to the previous block, making the ledger tamper evident. If data in an earlier block is changed, the cryptographic link to that block changes, and the change can be detected in later blocks. As new blocks are added, older blocks become more difficult to modify, creating tamper resistance. A blockchain network is the network in which a blockchain is used. Copies of the ledger are maintained across nodes in the network, and new blocks are added according to established validation and consensus rules. This distributed structure, together with cryptographic mechanisms, helps make the blockchain resilient to later attempts to alter the ledger. A born-and-bred Puerto Rican, with tattoos on her arms ranging from Gabriel García Márquez quotes to Peanuts characters, historian Laura set up her guiding company in 2022 to share her country’s “less-known stories, good or bad”. The salt flats are about 12 miles long and 5 miles wide and are comprised mostly of sodium chloride, or table salt. Located 120 miles west of Salt Lake City in Tooele County, Utah, the salt flats are a 30,000 acre expanse of hard, white salt crust on the western edge of the Great Salt Lake Basin in Utah. Like the Great Salt Lake, the Salt Flats are a remnant of Lake Bonneville, which covered over one-third of Utah from 10,000 to 32,000 years ago. The salt flats are on the National Register of Historic Places, are designated as an Area of Critical Environmental Concern, and are managed as a Special Recreation Management Area. The salt flats are generally open to the public for recreational purposes. Motor vehicle use is limited by seasonal closure during the spring when the salt is moist or has standing water on the surface. Closure dates may vary and will be posted by sign. Close booktiger's Diary [转载]可不能“随手一标”！ Posted by booktiger on 17 October 2026 in Chinese (China) (‪中文(中国大陆)‬) . 可不能“随手一标”！ 来源：国家安全部 2026年10月17日07:03 北京 https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/Xri2QFc-6VPpZ6QLBaqjgw 一张看似普通的网络地图，一个出于“兴趣”的随手标注，竟可能危害国家秘密安全。近年来，随着地理信息技术的普及，“开放地图”平台逐渐走入公众视野，但其背后隐藏的国家安全风险却不容忽视。 一个“爱好”带来的麻烦 2021年，许某在社交媒体上被一张带有艺术风格的路网地图所吸引。出于好奇，他开始接触境外开放地图平台，并违法“翻墙”访问。许某凭借对居住地周边环境的了解，以及从互联网搜集的公开信息，开始在境外开放地图平台上标注各类地理信息，多次标注军队等涉密敏感单位的位置信息。国家安全机关发现许某违法行为后迅速采取行动，依法对其开展审查。面对审查，许某懊悔道：“我完全没想到，自己只是出于爱好做点标记，竟会触犯法律，威胁国家安全。”国家安全机关向其宣讲了相关法律法规，讲明了其行为的危害性，并依法对其进行处理。许某表示已深刻认识到错误，并积极配合消除隐患。 随手一标，隐患巨大 “开放地图”一般指数据开源、可自由使用与编辑的地图项目，经常由全球志愿者共同创建、编辑并免费共享地理数据，在碳中和、城乡交通建设、灾害风险评估研究等方面具备相应应用价值。但如果在开放地图平台上标注我国涉密敏感地理信息，就有可能被不法分子利用，对我国家安全造成危害。不法分子无需动用复杂的技术手段，仅凭开放地图便能轻易获取我国涉密敏感单位的位置、规模等信息，并据此在军事基地等涉密敏感单位附近开展“黑飞”、偷拍、测绘等活动。境外间谍情报机关还可能结合其他渠道获取的信息进行多源数据交叉比对，拼凑成完整情报，甚至还可能对涉密单位工作人员以及周边居民、商户等人员开展针对性的渗透、拉拢和策反活动，对我国家安全构成严重威胁。 国家安全机关提示 《 中华人民共和国保守国家秘密法 》《 中华人民共和国测绘法 》《 公开地图内容表示规范 》等法律法规划出清晰底线：个人或者组织非法获取、持有、提供、利用属于国家秘密的地理信息的，将被依法追责。开放地图不是个人兴趣的“涂鸦板”，看似无心的标注可能触碰国家秘密“红线”。 ——绷紧“安全弦”。增强国家安全意识，不在地图平台标注任何涉及军事基地、涉密单位的地理信息。 ——把好“出口关”。不在社交平台发布涉密场所周边照片、视频，拍照前留意背景是否涉及敏感场所，不转发、不扩散任何标注有涉密地理信息的地图内容。 ——当好“守护者”。如发现在公开地图标注涉密地理信息等危害国家安全的可疑情况，请及时通过12339国家安全机关举报受理电话、网络举报受理平台（ www.12339.gov.cn ）、国家安全部微信公众号举报受理渠道或者直接向当地国家安全机关进行举报。 Discussion Leave a comment Log in to leave a comment

pages.text: Boxing: Jorge Linares remains in ICE detention and facing deportation - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Linares fought 56 times in his professional boxing career By Mandeep Sanghera BBC Sport journalist Published 18 November 2026 Former three-weight world champion Jorge Linares remains in the custody of US immigration authorities in Texas and is facing deportation. The 41-year-old Venezuelan was detained on Sunday when US Border Force and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers arrested him at El Paso International Airport. "On October 26, 2023, he entered the country with permission to stay for a temporary period, but in defiance of our nation's laws, he overstayed his welcome. He will remain in ICE custody pending removal proceedings," said an ICE spokesperson. "To be clear, a pending application or work authorisation does not confer legal status in the United States." Linares is based in Miami and has fought more than 10 times in America. The immigration law firm Wilner & O'Reilly are representing Linares and they denied their client was in the US illegally. "Mr Linares is authorised to be in the United States and he has cooperated fully with immigration authorities," said a Wilner & O'Reilly statement. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Br-12 Watchable Wildlife | Montana View Map In Full Screen This 200-acre prairie marsh in north central Montana holds a narrow reservoir about one mile long. This reservoir acts as a prairie pothole with its tailwaters slowly drying during the summer and fall. This water cycle permits waterfowl to hatch and raise young in this relatively isolated, resource-rich area, then move fledglings to major waters like the Missouri River. BR-12 also provides habitat for migrating waterfowl, upland birds, and upland wildlife species, so it’s not uncommon to observe 20-30 species in one spring day. Canvasback and redhead ducks regularly nest in the tailwaters, pelicans and tundra swans stop by for a rest and snack on their journeys, and even black terns (a species of concern) and loons have been observed utilizing BR-12’s “waterfowl facilities.” The area around BR-12 is short-grass prairie habitat. Species you might see associated with this habitat include chestnut-collared and McCowan’s longspur, horned lark, northern harrier, ferruginous hawk, Swainson’s hawk, burrowing owl, pronghorn, coyote, red fox, ground squirrel, and badger. I run Aloe Energy, a small not-for-profit initiative working on energy access in Sub-Saharan Africa. We published a free interactive map of the Southern African Power Pool grid, and OpenStreetMap is its backbone, so I wanted to share how it was built and where OSM could use help. What we did. We took every OSM power line of 66 kV and above across the 12 SAPP countries (country extracts from November 2026). Where OSM had no line but an older public map did, we filled the gap from TANESCO (2015) and World Bank (2017) grid maps, but only for lines recorded as existing, with a known voltage, and more than about 3 km from any OSM line. A “Source and age” view on the map colors each line by where it comes from, so you can see exactly what is OSM and what is gap-fill. Where OSM is thin. Coverage is weakest in Tanzania, DR Congo and Angola. Those are the places where the map still leans on maps that are close to ten years old, and where new mapping would change the picture most. Substations named in national plans are often missing too. The map: https://aloeenergy.org/research/sapp-grid . By Avery Stonich Published June 7, 2016 • 6 min read I get my first hint of the Pantanal 's impressive biodiversity as soon as I get off the plane in Corumbá , Brazil. White splotches cover the tarmac like some sort of Rorschach test on steroids. Bird droppings, I come to realize. The tropical heat drapes over me like a wool blanket; the thick air carries the raw scents of nature, a mix of earthy and sour. Part national park, part UNESCO World Heritage site , the Pantanal is the world’s largest tropical wetland, covering over 70,000 square miles—an area the size of Washington State—in the smack-dab center of South America. Brazil can lay claim to most of the region, but, as nature recognizes no political boundaries, the Pantanal spills into neighboring Paraguay and Bolivia. And though it's often overshadowed by the Amazon rain forest to the north, the Pantanal quietly boasts the highest concentration of wildlife on the continent . Life in the Pantanal follows the ebb and flow of an epic ecosystem that pulses with the seasons like a beating heart. pages.text: Brian Mann : NPR Accessibility links Skip to main content Keyboard shortcuts for audio player Brian Mann Enlarge this image Nancie Battaglia/NPR Nancie Battaglia/NPR Brian Mann Correspondent, National Desk Brian Mann is NPR's first national addiction correspondent. He also covers breaking news in the U.S. and around the world. Mann began covering drug policy and the opioid crisis as part of a partnership between NPR and North Country Public Radio in New York. After joining NPR full time in 2020, Mann was one of the first national journalists to track the deadly spread of the synthetic opioid fentanyl, reporting from California and Washington state to West Virginia. After losing his father and stepbrother to substance abuse, Mann's reporting breaks down the stigma surrounding addiction and creates a factual basis for the ongoing national discussion. Mann has also served on NPR teams covering the Beijing Winter Olympics and the war in Ukraine. During a career in public radio that began in the 1980s, Mann has won numerous regional and national Edward R. Murrow awards. He is author of a 2006 book about small town politics called Welcome to the Homeland , described by T he Atlantic as "one of the best books to date on the putative-red-blue divide." Mann grew up in Alaska and is now based in New York's Adirondack Mountains. His audio postcards, broadcast on NPR, describe his backcountry trips into wild places around the world. Photograph by Sussex News; Alamy By Orla Thomas Last updated November 1, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). ‘Remember, remember, the fifth of November’, goes the old nursery rhyme, ‘gunpowder, treason and plot.’ It’s a memorably succinct summary of the events of that very night in 1605, when Catholic rebel Guy Fawkes tried to blow up the Houses of Parliament and assassinate England’s Protestant king, James I. The monarch’s survival has been marked ever since and celebrations have evolved over the centuries. Traditionally, Guy’s effigy was burned on bonfires across the land, but now fireworks are the most common means of commemorating his failed — yet infamous — explosives attempt. Whichever event you choose, snack on beloved seasonal accompaniments — such as baked potatoes or toffee apples — as the dark skies over Britain become a blaze of colour. The tradition of carrying burning, tar-coated barrels through the streets of Ottery St Mary in Devon is a centuries-old tradition. Photograph by Steve Davey Photography; Alamy 1. The official sign on the banks of the River Tone at French Weir Park in Taunton advises people not to swim. The man, who has not been identified, landed at RAF Northolt before being transported to a specialist infectious diseases unit at the Royal Free Hospital in north London.
